text:
Lee: Quick one — trying to get the sample-app (node) working with redwoodctl local serve and ran into a confusing credential behavior.
Nora: What happened?
Lee: I followed the quickstart. Did `redwoodctl auth login` as my dev user, ran sample-app, but the app kept getting 401s intermittently. Local serve logs say it tried profile "default@cli" then fell back to an env profile.
DevQA: Intermittent 401s often mean multiple profiles or env vars clobbering each other. What does `REDWOOD_PROFILE` and `REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH` look like?
Lee: I didn't set them. Turns out the sample-app starter script exports REDWOOD_PROFILE=sample because of an older tutorial snippet in our repo.
Nora: Ah. So the CLI had a per-user ~/.redwood/profiles.json with one token, and the app was forcing a different profile that had an expired refresh token.
Lee: Correct. The weird bit is redwoodctl's auth retry: when the refresh fails it retries with exponential backoff but then silently switches to the env profile if present. Hard to debug.
DevQA: This is a DX problem: the CLI should log a clear line when it switches profiles and when a refresh fails with the offending profile id/uid. Right now it's buried in debug output.
Lee: Repro steps I used: clone sample-app, npm i, start redwoodctl auth login, run `node server.js` — saw the 401s in browser.
DocWriter: Can you paste the minimal log snippet (redacted)?
Lee: sure:
```
2026-01-17T11:02:10Z auth: refresh token for profile default@cli failed: expired_refresh_token
2026-01-17T11:02:10Z auth: retrying refresh (attempt 1)
2026-01-17T11:02:12Z auth: refresh token failed: unauthorized
2026-01-17T11:02:12Z config: env REDWOOD_PROFILE=sample detected, switching active profile
2026-01-17T11:02:12Z fs: load /home/lee/.redwood/profiles.json ok
2026-01-17T11:02:12Z auth: using profile sample (token expired)
2026-01-17T11:02:12Z runtime: request failed: 401 unauthorized
```
DevQA: Thanks. Suggested fixes: (1) surface a non-debug log when switching profiles because of env vars, (2) include profile identifier in auth error messages, (3) offer `redwoodctl auth doctor` which scans for multiple profiles with stale tokens and suggests `--merge` or `--remove`.
Nora: Also think about a safe default: if a refresh fails, don't fallback to another profile without explicit consent. That behavior surprised Lee.
DocWriter: I'll amend the quickstart to warn about exported REDWOOD_* env vars in the sample scripts. We can add a note in the migration guide about profile precedence: CLI arg > env > per-user profiles > system config.
Lee: Workaround that fixed it: `unset REDWOOD_PROFILE` then `redwoodctl auth login --reinit --profile sample` and restart local serve. Immediate green.
DevQA: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5481 "improve profile precedence visibility and auth error messages" (labels: devex, docs)
build-bot: CI run for sample-app (PR #834) failed: 401 on integration test (flaky).
Nora: I'll add a CI step to explicitly unset REDWOOD_PROFILE in the test harness and update the sample-app template.
DocWriter: I'll write the docs blurb + quick command examples showing how to inspect profiles: `redwoodctl auth list --verbose` and the new `redwoodctl auth doctor` (pending PR).
Lee: thanks everyone — little UX quirk but glad it's actionable.
